newsitem.title: LEBANON: Hariri's 30-yr bonds plan stuns Lebanon ministers.
newsitem.headline: Hariri's 30-yr bonds plan stuns Lebanon ministers.

text.p: Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri, worried by renewed signs of social unrest in Lebanon, has proposed that the government issue 30-year dollar-denominated treasury bonds to finance emergency social spending.
Hariri stunned government ministers by proposing a $1 billion 30-year issue at a routine Wednesday night cabinet meeting, newspapers said.
The maximum term of t-bonds that Lebanon currently issues is two years.

Newspapers said the proposal caused an uproar and two ministers walked out saying it would impose an intolerable tax burden on the country for 30 years. No decision was reached and a further meeting will be held on the issue.
If approved by the government, the proposal will require authorisation from parliament where foreign debt is a highly controversial issue among the 128 deputies.

Hariri's proposal followed the launch last week of a civil disobedience campaign in the eastern Bekaa Valley by a radical Shi'ite Moslem sheikh to pressure the government to alleviate what he says is hunger and poverty in the region.

The unrest in the Bekaa follows prolonged complaints by labour unionists, the media and opposition politicians that Hariri has ignored the plight of the poor in its multi-billion dollars drive to rebuild Lebanon.

The government, which has expressed concern about Sheikh Sobhi Tufaili's "hunger revolt", has already announced emergency funding of $100 million for the Bekaa, but Hariri told the cabinet on Wednesday he wanted to increase this to $400 million.
He also proposed extra funding totalling $600 million for education, medical care, south Lebanon and the return home of civil war refugees.
The 30-year t-bonds were designed to find a way round the government's chronic cash shortage which has already caused a soaring public debt and massive recurring budget deficits.

Public debt reached 22,622 billion Lebanese pounds ($14.7 billion) in May, close to the level of estimated GDP (Gross Domestic Product). The budget deficit of government income to expenditure was 56.3 percent for the first five months of the year compared with a 36 percent target for the year.

Banking sources told Reuters the bonds proposal was worked out at a meeting last week between Hariri, President Elias Hrawi, Bank of Lebanon Governor Riad Salameh and acting finance minister Fouad Siniora.
"It was prepared in a very secretive way at a meeting between them last week on this issue," a banker said. "I have a feeling it will be sold in the United States mainly," he said.
Lebanon currently holds weekly auctions of dollar-denominated treasury bills and bonds ranging from six months to two years.
Beirut financiers say the government has been preparing to issue three-year bonds for some time, but there has been no previous mention of 30-year bonds.
